history.period: Disputed: 19th century (temple trust) / 1971–72 (documented Nabakalebara) / some sources claim 12th century
history.summary: Sabara Srikhetra on the Nilasaila (Nisan Pabli) hillock in Koraput town is Odisha's famous 'Second Jagannath Temple', named for the Sabara/Savara tribe — the indigenous community whose chief Viswabasu is held to have first worshipped Jagannath as Nilamadhava before the Puri temple existed. CONSTRUCTION DATE CONFLICT (flagged): the temple trust's own site (sabarasrikhetra.com) dates it to the 19th century; travel blogs (Amazing Tour India, Eorissa Tourism) say it was built in 1972/the 1970s; Odisha Lifestyle and Velpu claim the 12th century. The best-documented fact is the 1969–71 Nabakalebara (reported by The New Indian Express via Hindu Blog): the three idols were carved in 1971 from leftover Daru (holy neem timber) of Lord Balabhadra's Puri idols, donated by the Puri SJTA and Gajapati Maharaj; since then Nabakalebara has not been observed here for lack of Puri daru. By 1982 all side deities were established. The ~50-ft, Kalinga-style, east-facing temple (Deula, Jagamohana, Nata Mandapa, Bhoga Mandapa) is approached by 100+ steps and is a symbol of equality — open to all castes, creeds and religions, with tribal priests performing rituals. The trust runs a Council of Analytical Tribal Studies, a tribal museum and pilgrim accommodation. Note: this row has no overlap with seq 2487 (a West Bengal duplicate), only with the Koraput temple sources.

town_description: Koraput is a hill town in southern Odisha's Eastern Ghats (~3,000 ft above sea level), the headquarters of Koraput district and the cultural heart of the undivided Koraput tribal region — known for its weekly tribal markets, the HAL engine division, coffee gardens and surrounding waterfalls.
